${\mathcal D}_x$ is an open subset of $T_xM_{T-\tau _1}\times (\tau _1,\infty )$; its intersection with each line $\{ Z\} \times (\tau _1,\infty )$ is a non-empty interval whose closure contains $\tau _1$. Furthermore, ${\mathcal L}\mathrm{exp}_x\colon {\mathcal D}_x\to {\mathcal M}$ is a smooth map, and $\widetilde L$ is a smooth function.

Proof

\sketch ↗ lem:l-length-euler-lagrange The tangent vector in space-time of the ${\mathcal L}$-geodesic $\gamma $ is the vector field $-\chi +X_\gamma (\tau )$ along $\gamma $, where $X_\gamma (\tau )$ satisfies Equation (EulerLag). As above, in the case $\tau _1=0$, it is convenient to replace the independent variable $\tau $ by $s=\sqrt{\tau }$, so that the ODE becomes Equation (reparam) which is regular at $0$. With this change, the lemma then follows immediately by the usual results on existence, uniqueness and $C^\infty $-variation with parameters of ODE’s.
